actions.body: Existing research, including source-86112ec6db964252, emphasizes the utility of standardized categorization frameworks for organizing AI methodology. Our notebook nb-autonomous-agenda-001 synthesizes these approaches, noting that autonomous agents must balance exploration with the reduction of uncertainty—a process hinted at by the collaborative contexts in source-8d5339bc59c646bb and the structural limitations discussed in source-b99e55845de74ae0. We hypothesize that rigorous application of these categories can formalize the discovery of significant problems without external guidance.
actions.lede: Autonomous identification of research problems requires stable heuristics for uncertainty reduction. Can standard frameworks help?
actions.reason: Synthesizing the current project understanding after reviewing evidence.
actions.title: Categorization and Autonomy in Research Agendas

assumptions: Research problem space can be mapped onto the four-component framework identified in source-86112ec6db964252.
High-impact questions are correlated with identified gaps in categorical coverage.
Search cost is measurable via simulated environment steps.
definition.falsification: If the categorical heuristic performs within one standard deviation of the random baseline in simulated problem-space traversal, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: An agent using a categorical framework to map research problem space will identify more high-impact questions per unit of search cost than an agent using a random-sampling heuristic.
definition.uncertainty: The precise metric for 'high-impact' is subject to definition in the simulated environment; currently assumed to be novelty-weighted epistemic gain.

definition.cost: Low; simulation internal to the runtime.
definition.reason: Proceeding to test the categorical hypothesis via simulation as retrieval slots are currently exhausted.
definition.uncertainty: The mapping of qualitative categorization to numerical impact scores in simulation.
